clue.text: Put money in oil-well in a depression

indicators.note: Put, paired with the later in, tells us to place one piece inside another
in, after Put, says the money goes within the oil-well

parts.note: a sump is the well or reservoir holding a car engine's oil
L, from Latin librae, is the abbreviation for pounds, i.e. money

explanation.surface: An investor sinks cash into an oil well just as the economy goes into a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put ... in' places L inside SUMP. 'Oil-well' looks like a drilling site, but here it is the sump of an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A slump is an economic downturn, which is what a depression is.

clue.text: Cutting off, the 'parson's retreat where spirits are invoked

indicators.note: where tells us the reversed clergyman is placed within the spirit-raising session

parts.note: a seance is a meeting at which the spirits of the dead are called up

indicators.note: retreat means going backwards, so the parson's title is read in reverse

parts.note: Rev is the abbreviated title of a parson

explanation.surface: A clergyman's sanctuary is cut off, the place where ghosts are summoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' looks like a refuge for the parson, but it signals going backwards; 'where' then places that piece within the spirit-raising session.
explanation.definitionFit: Severance is the act of severing, i.e. the cutting of a connection.

clue.text: Family man helps to keep the fun clean

indicators.note: the two words fun and clean together keep the answer within them

explanation.surface: A father figure helps keep the fun wholesome.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle is a male relative, a parent's brother.

clue.text: Capital fellows for getting plastered?

parts.note: men of the French capital, whose city's name is attached to a kind of plaster used for casts

explanation.surface: Great chaps for going out and getting drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastered' suggests drunkenness, but plaster of Paris is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of Paris, France's capital, which gives its name to plaster of Paris.

clue.text: Man's harlequinade part in Act VI

definitions.text: Man's harlequinade part in Act VI

parts.words: Man's harlequinade part in Act VI
parts.note: the foolish old man of the harlequinade, who is also the figure of the sixth age in Jaques's 'seven ages of man' speech

explanation.surface: An actor's role in the sixth act of some knockabout pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: In As You Like It, Jaques says man's life has seven 'acts'; the sixth 'shifts into the lean and slipper'd' old fool. That stock figure is also a character in the harlequinade, a traditional comic pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: The old dotard of the commedia-derived harlequinade is the same stock figure Shakespeare gives the sixth age of life.

clue.text: Harvest for Mussolini ?.

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
Il Duce, the leader, was Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: A crop gathered in for the Italian dictator.
explanation.definitionFit: Produce is the crop or yield that a harvest brings in.

clue.text: Nothing shot in the south east, and the lunch, is beastly

parts.note: no can mean none, nothing
a bag is the quantity of game shot

explanation.surface: No game was shot down in the south east and the lunch was awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' looks like a complaint about the food, but it means the lunch is for a beast: a horse's feedbag.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosebag is the bag of feed hung on a horse's head, an animal's portable meal.

clue.text: A woeful deficiency

parts.note: a lack is a deficiency or shortage

explanation.surface: A sad shortage.
explanation.definitionFit: Alack is an old cry of sorrow or regret.

clue.text: The potato she mashed for Mr Bones

indicators.note: mashed, as potato is, means the letters of potato she are crushed into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman mashes potato for her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mr Bones' sounds like a name, but it is a person who works on bones.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath treats the body by manipulating bones and joints.

clue.text: Frenchwoman's fabric

definitions.meaning: a French female name, with the 's standing for is
a sheer lightweight silk or nylon material

explanation.definitionFit: Ninon is a French girl's name, as in Ninon de Lenclos, and also a fine sheer dress material.

clue.text: Churchman with liabilities on behalf of another

parts.note: a vicar is a Church of England parish priest
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debt, so liabilities

explanation.surface: A clergyman with debts acting on someone else's account.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done vicariously is experienced or performed in place of another person.

clue.text: Play being performed in London

parts.note: to play a part is to act
a show that is being performed is on

explanation.surface: A theatre production currently running in the West End.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'in London': Acton is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Acton is a suburb within Greater London, so a place found in the capital.

clue.text: Classical thing about the Spanish dances

indicators.note: about means the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: res is Latin, the classical language, for thing
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Some antique object relating to Spanish dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classical' points to Latin, the language of the classics; 'about' signals one piece wrapped round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Reels are lively Scottish and Irish folk dances.

clue.text: Secretly right out of bunker, craftily won back point

indicators.note: craftily signals that the remaining letters are cunningly rearranged
out of means the letter for right is taken away from bunker
back means the word won is read in reverse

parts.note: N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A golfer sneakily chips out of a sand trap and wins back a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes R from BUNKER to leave BUNKE; 'craftily' turns that into UNBEK; 'back' turns WON into NOW; then add N.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbeknown describes something done without another's knowledge, hence covertly.

clue.text: Such leaves are never at variance

indicators.note: being at variance means being out of order, so the letters of never at are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some foliage is never in disagreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at variance' reads as the anagram signal, but 'at' is part of the fodder: rearrange NEVERAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervate is a botanical term for leaves that have visible veins or ribs.

clue.text: Main hazard-speed can get us tied up

parts.note: the main is the open sea, and a reef is a danger to shipping there
knots measure a ship's speed

explanation.surface: Danger at sea: going too fast can leave us stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Square knots used by sailors are for tying things securely.

clue.text: Closely related to a European egghead

parts.note: a German is a native of one European country
the head of the word egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: Someone is kin to a brainy continental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual, but it is read as the head of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: Germane means relevant or pertinent, i.e. closely connected to the matter.

clue.text: A bad case, in' tears, but gets up again

indicators.note: in puts the scrambled word inside the tears

parts.note: rends means tears, rips

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of case are spoilt and jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone with a terrible complaint is weeping but rises again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' suggests crying, but it is the verb to rip; 'bad' jumbles the word case, and 'in' sets the result inside. The opening 'A' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To reascend is to climb or rise once more.

clue.text: People paying Set, maybe …

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of paying set may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Worshippers offering homage to Set, the ancient god.
explanation.walkthrough: Set was an ancient god of the Nile kingdom, so the people paying homage to him are the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient worshippers of Set were the inhabitants of the Nile civilisation, a nation of people.

clue.text: Waldo might hold one in the act of coming out

indicators.note: might hold, paired with in, says this name would contain a letter to make the longer word, so we take that letter back out
in completes might hold: the letter would sit inside

parts.note: emersion is the act of emerging
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A man called Waldo might be clutching something during his emergence.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards from the clue: the name with I held inside it would be EMERSION, so removing the I from EMERSION gives the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was the American essayist, so Waldo is his middle name.

clue.text: … relating to their flower

parts.note: flower means something that flows, a river, here the great river of the people in the previous clue

explanation.surface: Concerning the national bloom of the people named before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' looks like a bloom but means 'something that flows', a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to the great African river.

clue.text: The lady may be mortal

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters of the lady could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman who is merely human.
explanation.definitionFit: Deathly can mean deadly or fatal, as in a deathly blow, matching mortal in the sense of mortal wound.

clue.text: Wanted to be, a schoolmaster indeed!

annotationWithheld.why: Wanted to be, a schoolmaster indeed! (7): DESIRED is SIR in DEED, but 'indeed' is both the container indicator (in) and the fodder (DEED), one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Wanted to be, a schoolmaster indeed!

clue.text: Starts another fire of a sort in 11 perhaps

indicators.note: in places the sort inside the rearranged dances
perhaps signals that the answer to 11 appears in an altered arrangement

parts.note: the answer to 11 across is the dances, REELS
a kind is a sort

explanation.surface: Someone sets a fresh blaze in some cross-referenced spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 11 means its answer; 'perhaps' jumbles that word to RELES, and 'in' sets the sort inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To rekindle is to light a fire again.

clue.text: Wiped out a bankrupt Anglo-Saxon

annotationWithheld.why: Wiped out a bankrupt Anglo-Saxon (5): RASED looks like AS inside RED, with 'bankrupt' doing two jobs (RED, in the red, and the breaking open); no parse with separate words found

clue.text: She may catch old soldiers

parts.note: to net is to catch
TA, the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: A woman who might snare some veterans.
explanation.definitionFit: Netta is a girl's name, so a woman referred to as she.

clue.text: Accountant takes the prize, for all his tricks

parts.note: CA, chartered accountant
the pot is the prize money in a card game

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper scoops the winnings, all thanks to his cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: A capot is the winning of every trick in the old card game piquet.
explanation.definitionFit: In piquet, taking every single trick of a deal is called a capot.

clue.text: Subaqueous god ?

parts.note: the Roman ruler of the underworld shares his name with the wartime fuel pipeline laid under the Channel

explanation.surface: A deity living beneath the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: The wartime acronym stood for Pipe-Line Under The Ocean, which supplied fuel across the Channel after D-Day.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of the underworld, and the code name of the undersea fuel pipeline of 1944.

clue.text: 'tis nothing " says the Athenian tinker

indicators.note: says signals that the phrase is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: 'tis nothing is 's nowt in Northern English dialect, nowt meaning nothing

explanation.surface: A craftsman from Athens shrugs off a remark.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Snout is the tinker among the Athenian workmen of A Midsummer Night's Dream. Said in dialect, ''s nowt' (it's nothing) gives his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Snout is the tinker among the rustic players in Shakespeare's comedy set near Athens.

clue.text: Poisonous creature, thanks to natural evolution

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks

indicators.note: evolution suggests change, so the letters of natural are reworked

explanation.surface: A venomous animal owes its existence to the natural process of evolution.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarantula is a large hairy spider with a venomous bite.

clue.text: Change to DC instead, when left far behind

indicators.note: Change tells us to alter the order of the letters in DC instead

explanation.surface: Electrical advice: switch to direct current instead when you have outrun the mains.
explanation.definitionFit: To be distanced is to be outpaced so that a gap opens up.

clue.text: Quiet operations in Oxford Street '

parts.note: sh is a call for silence
ops is short for operations

explanation.surface: Discreet surgery in a London shopping thoroughfare.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford Street is London's busiest shopping street, so the definition names what is found there.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford Street is lined with retail stores, so stores are what are found in it.
